title: How much does a sure mistake cost?
hook: How much does a model pay for being sure and wrong?

knows: that a model can give a chance to each possible answer
doesNotKnow: how the chance given to the true answer becomes a training penalty
that the penalty grows without limit as that chance goes to zero

misconception: A wrong answer costs the same whether the model was unsure or certain.
objective: The learner can explain that the penalty −ln(p) adds the same amount for every halving of the chance on the truth, so it climbs steeply and without limit as the model grows confidently wrong.

claims.text: −ln(0.5) = 0.69, −ln(0.1) = 2.30 and −ln(0.01) = 4.61, which is 6.6 times the 50% penalty.

Every halving of the chance on the truth adds the same 0.69 to the penalty; from 100%, 1% is about 6.6 halvings away, so it costs 6.6 times the first halving, and as the chance goes to 0% the penalty keeps rising without a ceiling.
claims.source: −ln(p/2) = −ln p + ln 2, ln 2 = 0.693; −ln p = ln 2 · log2(1/p), log2(100) = 6.64; −ln p → ∞ as p → 0. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 16): node: ln 2 = 0.6931; ln(100)/ln 2 = log2(100) = 6.644, shown as 6.6 (Q_ONE/Q_HALF); -ln p is unbounded as p -> 0. Stage halving chain from 50% adds 0.693 per step for nine steps. Advisory, non-blocking: the tenth tap clamps 0.098% to P_MIN 0.05% (not a true halving), adding 0.669, while the chain line still says 'each halving adds 0.69'.

claims.text: For one example, the cross-entropy penalty is ln(1 ÷ the probability the model gave the true class), which equals −ln of that probability. Classifiers are commonly trained to make it small, so confident mistakes cost far more than hedged ones; other penalties exist.
claims.source: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning, §6.2.1 (maximum likelihood / cross-entropy as the cost for classifiers) and §3.13. The 'far more' follows from c1-c2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 16): Derivation: cross-entropy H(q,p) = -sum q_i ln p_i with a one-hot q is -ln p_true = ln(1/p_true). 'Commonly trained to make it small': Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016 s6.2.1.1 (deeplearningbook.org unreachable from here); corroborated by Srihari CSE676 slides 6.2 (cedar.buffalo.edu, search snippet: cost is the negative log-likelihood, equivalently the cross-entropy between training data and model distribution). Hedge 'other penalties exist' is right. Reveal paragraph 3 matches.

claims.text: The stage shows one example's penalty, labelled 'One example' on the stage; real training averages it over many examples.
claims.source: Brief 38 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; Goodfellow et al. 2016 §6.2.1 (cost averaged over the training set).

recall.question: On one example, model A gave the true answer a 40% chance and model B gave it 2%. Under the −ln(p) penalty, which is penalised more?
options: A, because it was closer to 50%
They are penalised the same: both were wrong
recall.why: The penalty depends on the chance given to the truth: −ln 0.4 = 0.92, −ln 0.02 = 3.91. Being confidently wrong costs far more than hedging.
